talk: The money multiple tells you how many times your money grew. IRR (internal rate of return) tells you how fast, as a yearly rate. A shortcut: money doubles in about 72 divided by the yearly percentage, the rule of 72.

terms.meaning: Money back divided by money in. Also called MOIC.
The yearly growth rate that turns money in into money back.
Years to double is about 72 divided by the yearly percentage.

questions.prompt: Fund A turns $10M into $20M in 4 years. Fund B turns $10M into $20M in 8 years. Which has the higher IRR?
questions.hint: Same multiple. Who got there faster?
working: Both have a money multiple of $20M / $10M = 2.
Fund A got there in half the time, so its yearly rate is much higher.
whyNot: Same money, twice the wait. A slower double is a lower yearly rate.
Same multiple, but IRR is about speed. A got there in 4 years, B in 8.
You can tell: same start, same end, different time.

questions.prompt: Using the rule of 72, roughly what yearly return doubles money in 4 years?
whyNot: 100% / 4 = 25% spreads the gain evenly, but returns compound. Use 72 / 4 = 18.
50% a year would more than double money in 2 years.

questions.prompt: Using the rule of 72, about how many years does money take to double at 12% a year?
whyNot: 3 years would need a 24 percent return: 72 / 3 = 24.
9 years would mean 72 / 9 = 8 percent a year. You have 12%.
12 is the rate, not the years.

penalty.prompt: Money grows {rate}% a year. Using the rule of 72, about how many years does it take to double?

call.title: Quick money or more money
call.prompt: You have $1M to put into one club project. A pop-up fan festival pays back $1.5M within 5 matchdays. A hotel partnership pays back $1.8M, but only after a full season. Or do nothing.

options.label: The fan festival
options.result: Good call. $1.5M / $1M = 1.5 times in 5 matchdays beats $1.8M / $1M = 1.8 times over a full season, because the faster money can go to work again. That's what IRR measures.

options.label: The hotel partnership
options.result: More dollars in the end, but your money is stuck for a whole season. A bigger multiple can be the worse deal when it takes far longer.

takeaway: Money multiple says how much. IRR says how fast. Investors care about both.
